By applying dimensional analysis, a more rigorous understanding of Newton's law can be achieved, revealing the necessity of a gravitational constant, G. This constant, in conjunction with the speed of light, c, and the gravitational mass of a body, M, can be used to derive the Schwarzschild radius, a fundamental concept in general relativity. This simplified derivation, made possible by dimensional analysis, allows for a more intuitive understanding of the concept, without the need for complex calculations. This approach also enables the derivation of the Schwarzschild radius for various celestial bodies, such as the Sun, Earth, and the Milky Way, as well as the derivation of the Hubble radius, a fundamental concept in cosmology. This approach, in addition to its utility in deriving the Schwarzschild radius, also provides a framework for understanding the relationship between gravitational and inertial mass, as well as the equivalence principle.
